prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

TEXT_A:
Green Party Manifesto 2024 – Summary (under 500 words)

Vision
- Tackle the cost-of-living and climate crises together: a faster, fairer transition to a zero‑carbon economy, strong public services, and reduced inequality funded by taxing wealth and pollution.

Health and Care
- NHS: End privatisation; rapid GP access; universal NHS dentistry; pay restoration; cut waiting lists. Extra funding: £8bn in year one, rising to £28bn by 2030; £20bn capital over five years; primary care uplift and diagnostics expansion; new cancer plan; mental health therapies within 28 days; counsellor in every school; assisted dying with safeguards; end new HIV cases by 2030.
- Social care: Free personal care; £20bn/year; fair pay and career paths for carers; “Gloria’s Law” for essential care supporters; disability benefits +5% and reform; £3bn to improve children’s social care.

Homes and Planning
- Build 150,000 new social homes/year; end Right to Buy; rent controls; end no‑fault evictions.
- Green homes guarantee: £29bn insulation for homes, £9bn low‑carbon heat, £4bn to upgrade public buildings, £7bn to adapt to heat; Passivhaus‑level standards for new builds; protect green spaces and Green Belt; empower councils on planning and empty homes.

Energy and Climate
- No new oil and gas; end fossil subsidies; carbon tax rising toward £500/t within a decade.
- Renewables: wind ~70% of electricity by 2030; targets of 80GW offshore wind, 53GW onshore, 100GW solar by 2035; end onshore wind ban; community ownership in new projects.
- Expand grid, storage, interconnectors; support green hydrogen; oppose new nuclear and phase out existing.

Economy and Tax
- Green investment: average £40bn/year (rail, retrofits, energy, water, industry, active travel).
- Public ownership of rail, water, and Big 5 retail energy suppliers.
- Fair taxes: wealth tax (1% >£10m, 2% >£1bn); align CGT and investment income with earnings; remove NI upper limit; reform inheritance and pension reliefs; property tax reform toward land value; windfall taxes; VAT shifts; clamp down on avoidance; borrow to invest.

Work and Welfare
- Repeal anti‑union laws; Charter of Workers’ Rights; £15 minimum wage; day‑one rights; 10:1 pay ratio cap; protect gig workers; move toward a four‑day week.
- Raise Universal Credit/legacy benefits by £40/week; end five‑week wait; scrap two‑child cap and bedroom tax; disability benefits +5%; uprate pensions; higher Carer’s Allowance; long‑term Universal Basic Income ambition.

Nature, Animals, Food
- Rights of Nature Act; 30% land/sea protected by 2030; nationalise water; Clean Air Act; Right to Roam; rewet peat, expand woodland; £3bn/year for nature restoration; ban destructive fishing in MPAs.
- Commission on Animal Protection; ban blood sports, badger cull, factory‑farming cruelties; phase out animal testing.
- Triple farm support; agroecology; reduce pesticides; expand UK horticulture; universal free school meals and breakfast clubs; local food partnerships; cut waste.

Education
- +£8bn for schools and +£2.5bn/year for safe buildings; end high‑stakes testing and Ofsted; SEND +£5bn; restore school nurses and counsellors.
- FE/skills: £12bn; restore EMA. HE: scrap tuition fees; restore grants; address pension pressures.

Transport
- Public transport first: subsidies to £10bn/year; £19bn/5 years for PT and active travel; renationalise rail; local control of buses; £2.5bn/year for cycleways/footpaths.
- Oppose new roads; road pricing; rapid EV transition with scrappage up to £5bn/year; end new ICE sales by 2027, phase out by 2035; 20mph default in built‑up areas.
- Aviation: frequent‑flyer levy; no airport expansion; ban domestic flights under 3‑hour rail alternatives.

Democracy, Rights, Migration
- Fair Politics Act: scrap voter ID; proportional representation; clean party funding; stronger lobbying and media transparency; replace Lords; votes at 16; defend HRA/ECHR; trans self‑ID.
- Migration: end hostile environment, NRPF and 10‑year route; safe asylum routes; right to work; simplify/at‑cost visas; end spousal income rules; voting rights for visa holders.

Culture, Digital, Justice, World
- £5bn for community arts/sport; VAT relief on culture; media ownership caps; complete Leveson; Digital Bill of Rights; precautionary AI regulation and creator IP protection.
- Policing: rebuild trust; end routine stop‑and‑search and facial recognition; misogyny as hate crime; decriminalise sex work; restorative justice; presumption against short prison terms; +£11bn for MoJ and legal aid.
- Foreign policy: uphold international law; support Ukraine; ceasefire and rights‑based solution in Israel‑Palestine; halt UK arms to Israel; increase aid to 1% GNI and climate finance to 1.5% by 2033; path to rejoin EU (customs union first, free movement, Erasmus); sign UN nuclear ban, cancel Trident; reform NATO with no‑first‑use.

TEXT_B:
Reform UK’s 2024 “Contract with You” presents a rapid-change programme focused on cutting immigration, taxes and regulation; overhauling public services; expanding domestic energy; and constitutional shifts to assert UK sovereignty. The party frames the plan as an alternative to Conservatives and Labour, aiming to “take back control” of borders, money and laws.

Core pledges
- Freeze non‑essential immigration and “stop the boats.”
- Eliminate NHS waiting lists while keeping care free at point of use.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000 to “make work pay.”
- Scrap Net Zero policies and unlock UK oil and gas to cut bills.

Immigration
- Freeze non‑essential visas; create a Department of Immigration.
- Detain and deport illegal entrants; leave the ECHR if needed; process offshore; bar asylum from safe countries.
- Immediate deportation of foreign criminals; restrict student dependants; five‑year residency for benefits.
- Employer immigration tax (higher NI for foreign hires, with exemptions).

Government waste
- Stop Bank of England interest on QE reserves; 5% departmental efficiency drive; cut EU‑era rules; halve foreign aid; improve HMRC collection.

Economy (personal)
- Lift income tax start to £20k; higher rate from £70k.
- Cut fuel duty by 20p; scrap VAT on energy and green levies.
- Big stamp duty cuts; restore VAT‑free tourist shopping.
- IHT abolished below £2m; 20% rate above.

Economy (business)
- Raise corporation tax threshold to £100k; cut main rate to 20%, then 15%.
- Abolish IR35; lift VAT threshold to £150k.
- Abolish business rates for high‑street SMEs, offset with 4% online delivery tax.
- Looser employment rules; faster planning; major tax simplification.

NHS
- Zero basic‑rate income tax for NHS/care staff for 3 years; expand UK training and write off fees with service.
- Use independent capacity; 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance.
- Patient vouchers if GP/consultant/operation waits exceed 3/3/9 weeks.
- Efficiency drives; pharmacy‑first approach; inquiry into excess deaths/vaccine harms.

Net Zero/energy
- Scrap Net Zero and renewable subsidies; fast‑track North Sea and shale trials.
- Expand nuclear SMRs and other technologies.

Policing and justice
- 40,000 extra officers; zero‑tolerance approach; more stop and search; end DE&I roles.
- Increase justice budget; redefine hate crime; 10,000 new prison places; mandatory life for repeat violent offenders.

Education
- “Patriotic” curriculum; ban transgender ideology in schools; 20% tax relief on independent school fees.
- Scrap interest on student loans; tougher university standards; protect free speech; expand PRUs; offer 2‑year degrees.

Welfare
- Stronger work requirements (two‑strike rule); face‑to‑face assessments.

Brexit/sovereignty
- Scrap retained EU law; abandon Windsor Framework; prepare TCA renegotiation; distance from EU defence ties.

Defence
- Spend 2.5% of GDP by year 3, 3% by year 6; pay rises; new justice bill; veterans department; recruit 30,000; procurement reform.

Housing
- Fast‑track brownfield; prioritise locals in social housing; restore mortgage interest relief for landlords; drop Renters’ Reform Bill; protect leaseholders.

Families
- Transferable marriage allowance (aiming at 25%); front‑load child benefit for ages 1–4; single‑sex spaces; tackle social media harms.

Transport/utilities
- Scrap HS2; ban ULEZ/LTNs/most 20mph zones; invest in existing roads/rails.
- New ownership model: 50% public, 50% UK pension funds; cap standing charges.

Agriculture/fishing
- Boost farm budget; scrap climate‑linked subsidies; protect country sports; curb supermarket power; buy British.
- Restrict foreign access to UK waters; expand patrols; ban supertrawlers; rebuild processing and fleets.

Pensions/social care
- Royal Commission on social care; curb offshore tax avoidance in care; pension reforms; fix Mineworkers’ scheme.

Constitution/culture
- Leave ECHR; reform Lords and civil service; tighten postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights.
- Reject WHO treaty/WEF/CBDC; replace Equalities Act; free speech bill; scrap BBC licence fee; national holidays; anti‑corruption unit.

Funding (party estimates)
- Annual savings: ~£150bn plus £10bn from extra growth = £160bn.
- Annual costs: ~£141bn.
